answer: I'd like to describe a small moment of kindness that happened in the main market in Sirajganj a few months ago. A time I helped a stranger was when I came across an elderly man who had stumbled and dropped his shopping on a busy street. There were vegetables and a bag of rice spread across the road, and rickshaws were [[weaving around]] him. Most people simply walked past, which I found rather [[disheartening]]. I stopped to help him gather his things and made sure he was not hurt. Luckily, apart from a small scrape on his hand, he was fine. He seemed a little shaken, so I stayed with him for a few minutes and offered to walk him to a nearby bench outside a tea stall. He was incredibly grateful, and we ended up having a lovely short chat; it turned out he was a retired schoolteacher who now lived alone, since his children had moved to Dhaka for work. What struck me was how such a small gesture clearly meant a great deal to him. Honestly, it took only a couple of minutes of my time, yet it felt genuinely meaningful. It reminded me that we often overlook small chances to be kind because we are so [[caught up in]] our own lives. That brief encounter left me feeling [[heartened]] for the rest of the day, and it made me more [[attentive]] to people around me who might need help. I still see him in the market sometimes, and he always waves.

followUps.q: Do you think people help strangers less than in the past?
followUps.answer: In big cities, perhaps. Everyone is in a hurry and slightly wary of strangers. In smaller towns like mine, people still tend to stop, although even here I notice it happening less.

followUps.q: Has anyone ever helped you when you were a stranger somewhere?
followUps.answer: Yes, when I got lost in Chattogram once, a shopkeeper drew me a little map and pointed me in the right direction. I have never forgotten how kind he was.

note: Set in Sirajganj market with rickshaws; added who the stranger was (retired teacher living alone); plain marks 'grateful' and 'meaningful' replaced by 'caught up in', 'heartened', 'weaving around'.
